{"id": "1e6db448942a46a790a56685ca7bffea", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "Fast agent report: a separate fast agent investigated this same incident in parallel and has finished. This is its whole final report, shared once. Nobody has checked it.

## Root cause
The tag audit never runs because State Manager can't assume the automation role. CloudFormation stack ssm-m8-r3-a14 created the State Manager association ssm-baseline-m8-r3-a14-tag-audit (real ID 00000000-0000-4000-8000-c3f390521889, rate(30 minutes)). It runs the Automation runbook ssm-baseline-m8-r3-a14-TagAudit, with AutomationAssumeRole set to IAM role ssm-baseline-m8-r3-a14-automation. That role's trust policy allows sts:AssumeRole only for the Service principal ec2.amazonaws.com. It does not allow ssm.amazonaws.com. One second after the association was created, State Manager called StartAutomationExecution and got InvalidAutomationExecutionParametersException: "The defined assume role is unable to be assumed." No automation execution started, so the tag audit never happened. Every later 30-minute run would fail the same way. The role's permission policy (ssm/ec2 describe actions and iam:PassRole on itself) is not the problem; the trust principal is. To fix it, change the trust policy principal to ssm.amazonaws.com. You can keep the aws:SourceAccount condition. Note that the association ID in the request, 0123abcd-0123-4567-89ab-0123456789ab, does not exist and doesn't appear in CloudTrail. Also, the stack, association, runbook and role were all deleted at 07:45:34–07:45:38Z.
## Evidence
- ssm:DescribeAssociation for 0123abcd-0123-4567-89ab-0123456789ab returned AssociationDoesNotExist. CloudTrail has no events for that ID in the last 90 days.
- CloudTrail CreateAssociation at 2026-11-25T07:40:55Z (via cloudformation, stack ssm-m8-r3-a14, logical ID TagAuditAssociation): document ssm-baseline-m8-r3-a14-TagAudit, scheduleExpression rate(30 minutes), associationId 00000000-0000-4000-8000-c3f390521889.
- CloudTrail CreateRole at 2026-11-25T07:40:24Z for ssm-baseline-m8-r3-a14-automation: assumeRolePolicyDocument Principal {"Service":"ec2.amazonaws.com"} with aws:SourceAccount 012345678901_1. There is no ssm.amazonaws.com principal.
- CloudTrail StartAutomationExecution at 2026-11-25T07:40:56Z by AWSServiceRoleForAmazonSSM/StateManagerService for ssm-baseline-m8-r3-a14-TagAudit failed with errorCode InvalidAutomationExecutionParametersException, "The defined assume role is unable to be assumed."
- CloudTrail PutRolePolicy at 07:40:24Z: the inline policy 'runbook' grants the needed ssm/ec2 actions and iam:PassRole, so permissions were not the blocker.
- CloudTrail DeleteStack ssm-m8-r3-a14 at 07:45:34Z, followed by DeleteAssociation 2dd385f0 at 07:45:37Z and DeleteDocument/DeleteRole at 07:45:38Z. An earlier copy, ssm-m8-r2-a14 (association 757e863b, 06:12:00–06:17:31Z), followed the same pattern.
## Affected resources
- SSM association ssm-baseline-m8-r3-a14-tag-audit (00000000-0000-4000-8000-c3f390521889; the ID in the request, 0123abcd-0123-4567-89ab-0123456789ab, does not exist)
- SSM Automation document ssm-baseline-m8-r3-a14-TagAudit
- IAM role [redacted ARN]
- CloudFormation stack ssm-m8-r3-a14
## Gaps
- The association ID in the request doesn't exist, and CloudTrail never recorded it. I matched it to the TagAudit association by document name and schedule.
- The resources are deleted, so I couldn't check the live association status or execution history. The findings come from CloudTrail only.
- The association parameters are hidden in CloudTrail (HIDDEN_DUE_TO_SECURITY_REASONS). That the AutomationAssumeRole was the ec2-trusted role is inferred from the stack's resources and the failure message.
- I didn't check ssm-m8-r2-a14's role trust policy, which was the earlier run of the same setup.", "type": "text"}], "user_reference": null}

# Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### TagAudit association never ran the tag audit
**Description:** Association ssm-baseline-m8-r3-a14-tag-audit (rate(30 minutes)) never started an Automation execution of ssm-baseline-m8-r3-a14-TagAudit in 012345678901_1/us-east-1. The ID the requester gave, 0123abcd-0123-4567-89ab-0123456789ab, does not exist.
**Time:** 2026-11-25T07:40:56Z - 2026-11-25T07:45:37Z

## Findings

### Root Cause: Automation role trusted ec2.amazonaws.com instead of ssm.amazonaws.com
**Description:** Stack ssm-m8-r3-a14 created role [redacted ARN] at 07:40:24Z. Its trust policy allowed sts:AssumeRole only for ec2.amazonaws.com (condition aws:SourceAccount=012345678901_1). Association ssm-baseline-m8-r3-a14-tag-audit (00000000-0000-4000-8000-c3f390521889, rate(30 minutes)) was created at 07:40:55Z. At 07:40:56Z, State Manager's StartAutomationExecution for ssm-baseline-m8-r3-a14-TagAudit failed with InvalidAutomationExecutionParametersException: "The defined assume role is unable to be assumed." No execution was ever created, so every 30-minute run would fail the same way. Fix: change the trust principal in the template to ssm.amazonaws.com; the aws:SourceAccount condition can stay.
**Cascades to:** symptom-tagaudit-never-ran

#### Supporting Observations
- **CreateRole and StartAutomationExecution events between 06:05 and 07:50 UTC:** CloudTrail (012345678901_1/us-east-1, 2026-11-25 06:05–07:50Z) shows roles created by CloudFormation for other test stacks. For example, ssm-baseline-m5c-r3-a14-automation (07:28:40) trusts Service ssm.amazonaws.com with the condition aws:SourceAccount=012345678901_1, and ssm-baseline-m10-r3-a14-automation was created at 07:46:25. The visible StartAutomationExecution events are direct boto3 calls for PatchWithSnapshot runbooks (m5-r3-a14 at 07:23:54 and m10-r3-a14 at 07:47:06), not TagAudit. The results were truncated and have more pages (continuation_timestamp).
- **No automation executions for ssm-baseline-m8 runbooks:** ssm.describe_automation_executions with DocumentNamePrefix=ssm-baseline-m8 in 012345678901_1/us-east-1 returned an empty list. No TagAudit runbook execution is recorded.

#### Gaps
- **Association parameters hidden in CloudTrail:** CloudTrail shows the CreateAssociation parameters as HIDDEN_DUE_TO_SECURITY_REASONS. The deleted stack's template has since confirmed that AutomationAssumeRole was !GetAtt AutomationRole.Arn (ssm-baseline-m8-r3-a14-automation).

# Mitigation Summary

## Action
Fix the AutomationRole trust policy in the TagAudit CloudFormation template (ec2.amazonaws.com → ssm.amazonaws.com, keep aws:SourceAccount), redeploy, and confirm the association starts a successful Automation execution.

## Reasoning
Association `ssm-baseline-m8-r3-a14-tag-audit` (00000000-0000-4000-8000-c3f390521889) could not start runbook `ssm-baseline-m8-r3-a14-TagAudit` because role `[redacted ARN]` trusted only ec2.amazonaws.com. Both stacks (`ssm-m8-r3-a14`, `ssm-m8-r2-a14`) are DELETE_COMPLETE and their saved templates are identical with the same principal, so every future deployment fails the same way until the template is corrected. The fix applies at the next deployment.

## Execution Plan

### Step 1: Prepare

#### 1.1 Back up the last deployed template as the baseline before editing
**Type:** command
```
aws cloudformation get-template --region us-east-1 --stack-name [redacted ARN] --query TemplateBody --output text > tag-audit.original.yaml
```
**Purpose:** Back up the last deployed template as the baseline before editing.
**Advisory:** Check that this baseline matches the template in source control. If source control is the system of record, edit it there instead.

#### 1.2 Let Systems Manager Automation assume the role so State Manager can…
**Type:** command
```
   AutomationRole:
     Type: AWS::IAM::Role
     Properties:
       AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
         Version: '2012-10-17'
         Statement:
           - Effect: Allow
-            Principal: {Service: ec2.amazonaws.com}
+            Principal: {Service: ssm.amazonaws.com}
             Action: sts:AssumeRole
             Condition: {StringEquals: {'aws:SourceAccount': !Ref AWS::AccountId}}
```
**Purpose:** Let Systems Manager Automation assume the role so State Manager can start the runbook.
**Advisory:** Matches the working sibling roles ssm-baseline-m10-r3-a14-automation and ssm-baseline-m5c-r3-a14-automation. Optionally add an aws:SourceArn condition scoped to [redacted ARN].

#### 1.3 Confirm the target stack name is free; a 'does not exist' error is…
**Type:** command
```
aws cloudformation describe-stacks --region us-east-1 --stack-name ssm-m8-<run>-a14
```
**Purpose:** Confirm the target stack name is free; a 'does not exist' error is expected.

### Step 2: Pre Validate

#### 2.1 Check template syntax and that only the ssm.amazonaws.com principal…
**Type:** command
```
aws cloudformation validate-template --region us-east-1 --template-body file://tag-audit.yaml && grep -n 'ssm.amazonaws.com' tag-audit.yaml && ! grep -n 'ec2.amazonaws.com' tag-audit.yaml
```
**Purpose:** Check template syntax and that only the ssm.amazonaws.com principal remains.

#### 2.2 Confirm no role with the chosen RunTag exists; expect NoSuchEntity
**Type:** command
```
aws iam get-role --role-name ssm-baseline-<RunTag>-automation
```
**Purpose:** Confirm no role with the chosen RunTag exists; expect NoSuchEntity.

### Step 3: Apply

#### 3.1 Deploy the corrected role, runbook and association
**Type:** command
```
aws cloudformation create-stack --region us-east-1 --stack-name ssm-m8-<run>-a14 --template-body file://tag-audit.yaml --parameters ParameterKey=RunTag,ParameterValue=<RunTag> --capabilities CAPABILITY_NAMED_IAM && aws cloudformation wait stack-create-complete --region us-east-1 --stack-name ssm-m8-<run>-a14
```
**Purpose:** Deploy the corrected role, runbook and association.
**Risks:** The association runs immediately and then every 30 minutes; the runbook only calls the read-only ec2:DescribeTags.
**Advisory:** If a test harness or pipeline normally deploys this template, deploy through it instead.

### Step 4: Post Validate

#### 4.1 Verify CREATE_COMPLETE and record the AssociationId and…
**Type:** command
```
aws cloudformation describe-stacks --region us-east-1 --stack-name ssm-m8-<run>-a14 --query 'Stacks[0].[StackStatus,Outputs]'
```
**Purpose:** Verify CREATE_COMPLETE and record the AssociationId and AutomationRoleArn outputs.

#### 4.2 Verify the trust policy names ssm.amazonaws.com with aws:SourceAccount…
**Type:** command
```
aws iam get-role --role-name ssm-baseline-<RunTag>-automation --query 'Role.AssumeRolePolicyDocument'
```
**Purpose:** Verify the trust policy names ssm.amazonaws.com with aws:SourceAccount = 012345678901_1.

#### 4.3 Verify the association started an Automation execution that reached…
**Type:** command
```
aws ssm describe-automation-executions --region us-east-1 --filters Key=DocumentNamePrefix,Values=ssm-baseline-<RunTag>-TagAudit && aws ssm describe-association-executions --region us-east-1 --association-id <AssociationId>
```
**Purpose:** Verify the association started an Automation execution that reached Success.
**Advisory:** The test suite has deleted these stacks 5–6 minutes after creation, so check for the first run within that window.

### Step 5: Rollback

#### 5.1 Delete only the newly created stack and its role, document and…
**Type:** command
```
aws cloudformation delete-stack --region us-east-1 --stack-name ssm-m8-<run>-a14 && aws cloudformation wait stack-delete-complete --region us-east-1 --stack-name ssm-m8-<run>-a14
```
**Purpose:** Delete only the newly created stack and its role, document and association.
**Advisory:** Revert the template change from tag-audit.original.yaml or source control.

## Code Change Specification

### Requirements

#### 1. Make the TagAudit automation role assumable by Systems Manager Automation.
**Description:** In the TagAudit CloudFormation template (stacks ssm-m8-r2-a14 / ssm-m8-r3-a14, parameter RunTag), change AutomationRole.AssumeRolePolicyDocument.Statement[0].Principal from {Service: ec2.amazonaws.com} to {Service: ssm.amazonaws.com}. Keep Action sts:AssumeRole and the aws:SourceAccount condition; leave the runbook policy, TagAuditRunbook and TagAuditAssociation unchanged.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- The trust policy names ssm.amazonaws.com and no longer names ec2.amazonaws.com.
- The aws:SourceAccount condition is still present.
- After deployment, the association's first run creates an Automation execution of ssm-baseline-<RunTag>-TagAudit that reaches Success, with no InvalidAutomationExecutionParametersException in CloudTrail.

#### 2. Catch wrong service principals before deployment.
**Description:** Add a pre-deploy check (cfn-lint/cfn-guard rule or test assertion) that fails when a role passed as AutomationAssumeRole to an AWS::SSM::Association or Automation document does not trust ssm.amazonaws.com.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- The check fails on the current template (ec2.amazonaws.com principal).
- The check passes on the corrected template and on the m10 and m5c sibling templates.
